subtitle: Lesson 11 · System Design for Data Engineers

code:
POST /orders  {idempotency_key: "abc-123", ...}
-> creates order #4471, stores abc-123 -> #4471

Same request retried with abc-123 again
-> returns order #4471 -- no second order created
caption: A retry recognized as the same operation, not a new one.

code:
MERGE INTO FactOrders AS target
USING IncomingOrders AS source
ON target.order_id = source.order_id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *
caption: A reprocessed batch updates rows instead of duplicating them.

code:
Natural key:    order_id -- exists BEFORE it reaches you,
                stable across every retry
Surrogate key:  OrderSK -- generated fresh on load,
                NOT stable across attempts
caption: MERGE must match on the natural key to stay idempotent.

subtitle: Where idempotency turns out to be the real answer.
